subject: chemistry
title: Properties
textbookText: In graphite, each carbon atom is sp2 hybridized. Each carbon atom is covalently bonded to three other carbon atoms forming a hexagonal flat layer. Therefore, unlike diamond, graphite possesses two dimensional structures. The C-C bond length in graphite is 1.42Å and bond angle is 120 0. Each hexagonal sheet is held together by a weak Van der Waal force which makes graphite slippery. Since one valence electron of each carbon atom is free to move therefore graphite behaves as a good conductor of electricity.
a. It is a good conductor of electricity.
b. It possesses the ability to mark the paper. Therefore, it is used to prepare lead
c. It is lighter than diamond and is slippery to touch.
d. It is insoluble in water and other solvent.
f. It is soft due to the weak Van der Waal's force.
g. Its melting point is 3500 0C which is higher than diamond.
h. It is chemically inert. However, it burns on strong heating to produce CO2.
i. It is converted into diamond when heated at about 1600 0C and 50,000 - 60,000

Uses of Graphite a. It is used to make electrodes as it is a good conductor of electricity. b. It is used to prepare lead pencils. c. It is used as lubricants for machines working at high temperature. d. It is used to make crucibles (melting pots for extremely hot chemical reactions).
